record.what_it_does: Edge network, CDN, DNS, security, Workers serverless and developer platform.
record.subcategory: Cloud infrastructure / CDN and edge platform
record.auth_notes: Developers can now register their own OAuth clients in the dashboard (Manage Account > OAuth clients) or through the API. These clients use the Authorization Code flow, with PKCE for public clients. Scoped consent lets users deselect optional scopes. Client Credentials, Implicit, ROPC and Device grants are not supported for third-party clients. Scoped API tokens, user or account-owned and sent as a Bearer header, remain fully supported and suit single-tenant or CI use. The legacy Global API key (X-Auth-Email plus X-Auth-Key) is still accepted but discouraged. Origin CA keys cover certificate endpoints, recorded here as 'other'. A multi-user toolkit should use a public OAuth client.
record.access_notes: A free Cloudflare account can create API tokens and OAuth clients. The OAuth docs list availability as Yes on the Free, Pro, Business and Enterprise plans. A client starts as private, usable only by account members. To make it public for any Cloudflare user, you must verify ownership of the client domain with a DNS TXT record. The docs describe no manual app review. Some individual products and endpoints need paid plans or Enterprise, but core API access does not.
record.api_breadth_notes: The REST API has over 2,500 endpoints; the MCP docs say "over 2,500 endpoints" and list 2,594 tools. They cover zones, DNS, Workers, R2, D1, KV, Zero Trust, WAF, certificates, accounts and more. A GraphQL Analytics API is also available. The global rate limit is 1,200 requests per 5 minutes per user.
record.mcp_notes: The main server is https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. It provides search() and execute() tools across the whole API, plus docs(). It authenticates with OAuth, or with an API token sent as a bearer token. Optional product servers are docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, containers.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, browser.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, dex.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, casb.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp and agents.cloudflare.com/mcp.
record.blocker_notes: There is no real blocker. A public OAuth client needs only domain verification (a DNS TXT record), not a manual review. Webhooks are limited to Notifications alert delivery; there are no general resource-change event subscriptions. There is no separate sandbox, but a free account works as a test environment.
